one_liner: Archived Windows/MSVC zlib fork with SIMD hashing, CRC and match patches; about 1.3-1.9x zlib 1.2.11 level-6 compression.
what_it_does: A fork of madler/zlib (now at 1.2.13 per zlib.h) that keeps the zlib API and ABI and builds zlib1.dll for Win32, x64 and ARM64 from a Visual Studio project. It folds in third-party speed patches: Intel's PCLMULQDQ CRC-32 and SSE4.2 CRC32-instruction hashing, Cloudflare's and gildor2/fast_zlib's longest_match, Chromium's SIMD adler32, ARM CRC/adler patches, and (in 2022 commits) zlib-ng's chunkset inflate copy and compare256 code.
how_it_is_fast: On x86 with SSE4.2 the deflate hash is the hardware CRC32 instruction over 4 bytes with a fixed 15-bit hash table (insert_string_sse), and the window slide uses SSE2; on ARM64 the ACLE CRC32 hash is used unconditionally. longest_match is the fast_zlib/Cloudflare variant (compares several bytes at once, compare256), CRC-32 uses PCLMULQDQ folding, adler32 uses SSE/AVX2 or NEON, and inflate copies matches with zlib-ng's chunkset. CPU features are detected at run time (x86_check_features) on x86.
when_to_use: Windows applications that ship their own zlib1.dll built with MSVC and spend time in deflate level 6 (the measured case: 1.3-1.9x on silesia mozilla and webster).
Windows on ARM64 builds that want a zlib with CRC32 hashing and NEON adler32 under the stock zlib API.
As a reference for how the Intel, Cloudflare and fast_zlib deflate patches combine, before choosing a maintained fork.
when_not_to_use: Anything that needs maintenance or security fixes: the repository was archived on 2026-06-17, the last commit is 2025-02-21, and it is based on zlib 1.2.13, so upstream 1.3.x fixes (e.g. the minizip CVE-2023-45853 fix in 1.3.1) are absent.

Linux, macOS or GCC/Clang builds: there is no Makefile, configure or CMake at the root, only zlib.sln/zlib.vcxproj (toolset v143), crc32.c includes headers with Windows backslash paths, and SIMD paths are gated on MSVC macros (_M_IX86, _M_AMD64, _M_ARM64).

Old x86 CPUs without SSE4.2/PCLMUL: open issue #2 (2018, no maintainer reply) reports altered decompressed output (text 'becomes upper-cased') on an AMD CPU with only SSE4A; it was never confirmed or fixed.
Workloads that need byte-identical output with stock zlib: the CRC32 hash and fixed hash_bits produce different compressed streams (19,064,581 vs 19,089,124 bytes on mozilla).
New projects: zlib-ng and libdeflate (siblings) carry the same ideas, run on all major platforms and are maintained.

integration.dependencies: none (Visual Studio project; a 2023 commit links onecore.lib)
integration.min_toolchain: MSVC with platform toolset v143 (Visual Studio 2022), C17 (LanguageStandard_C stdc17); ARM64 target set to ARMv8.2
integration.platforms: Windows x86 (Win32), x64 and ARM64; SIMD paths need SSE2 (slide_hash), SSE4.2 for the CRC32 hash and PCLMUL for CRC-32, chosen at run time; other OSes not supported by the build files
integration.thread_safety: Same as zlib (README: 'All the code is thread safe' per stream); CPU-feature globals are set on deflateInit or crc32(0, NULL, 0) without synchronisation (benign write of identical values).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same zlib API and zlib1.dll name on Windows, so it replaces a Windows zlib DLL; compressed bytes differ from stock zlib, memLevel no longer sets the hash size when SSE4.2 or ARM64 is used, and some project configurations define ZLIB_CONST, which changes next_in to const.

gotchas: With SSE4.2 (and always on ARM64) hash_bits is forced to 15 regardless of memLevel, so memLevel tuning has no effect on the hash table.
crc32() called before any deflateInit or crc32(0, NULL, 0) sees CPU features as unset and takes the table path: correct but without the PCLMUL speedup.

The benchmark harness (zlib-perf perf.c) has a no-op verification: it compares 'checksum != checksum' and never uses checksum2, so '-v' only catches inflate errors; timing uses GetTickCount (10-16 ms resolution) and includes fread of the input file.

Results.md is internally inconsistent for one row: matbech/zlib x86 on mozilla lists 1234 ms but 47 MB/s, while the harness formula gives 39 MB/s for 1234 ms (every other row matches), so that speedup is about 1.47x by time, not 1.8x.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely: pick it only for a Windows-only MSVC build that must keep the stock zlib API and a single zlib1.dll and cannot adopt zlib-ng in compat mode. Otherwise zlib-ng (maintained, faster, same API in compat mode), libdeflate (faster whole-buffer API) or Cloudflare's zlib fork (the source of its longest_match patch) are better choices.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Results.md: compression only, level 6, two silesia files, MSVC 19.14 (VS 15.7) on a CPU written as 'i7 8770' (link is the i7-8700), timed with GetTickCount; by the listed times the fork took 1234/922 ms vs zlib 1.2.11's 1813/1718 ms on mozilla (x86/x64) and 1032/907 vs 1359/1313 ms on webster, i.e. 1.32-1.86x (derived from page data), with slightly smaller output. The measured binaries predate the current code (1.2.13 base, chunkset and AVX2 patches added in 2022), and zlib-ng was not measured on x64 because of a deflate bug at the time.
status_note: Abandoned: archived 2026-06-17, last commit 2025-02-21, 7 stars, 3 open issues including an unanswered correctness report; Zlib-licensed and copyable, but treat it as a patch reference rather than a dependency.
